content.title: Who is that 'Beef' star? The full Season 2 cast and how you know them
content.text: Get ready for another juicy helping of "Beef."Netflix's Emmy-winning drama about the petty clashes that turn into blood feuds has returned three years after its first season. This time, instead of two strangers viciously ruining each others lives over road rage (played by Season 1's Ali Wong and Steven Yeun), we have two different romantic couples at each others' throats over social and class politics at a swanky country club. Add in rich and callous club-goers, an enigmatic South Korean billionaire, an irresponsible plastic surgeon and a couple attractive home-wreckers, you have a story set up for the kind of cringey chaos that made the first go-round such a sensation.The Season 2 cast is led by household names Oscar Isaac and Carey Mulligan, playing a deeply unhappy husband and wife whose semi-violent fight sets off the series of wild events of the season.Here's a who's-who of the star-studded Season 2 crew and how you know them.Meet our unhappy couple: Carey Mulligan and Oscar Isaac as Lindsay and JoshAt the start of "Beef" Season 2 we meet Josh (Isaac), the general manager of a ritzy LA country club who desperately wants the power, money and prestige of the rich clients he serves drinks to every night. He's married to Lindsay (Mulligan), an interior decorator who resents her husband for squandering their dreams of opening a bed and breakfast. At home after a fundraiser one night at the club, the couple gets into an argument over finances, their dreams, their sex life, and seemingly every problem they've ever had. It starts to turn violent, with broken glasses and Josh grabbing a golf club to seemingly strike Lindsay. That's when they notice they're being watched.Carey Mulligan as Lindsay Crane-Martin in "Beef."Who is Carey Mulligan? The British actress has been nominated for an Oscar three times: In 2010 for "An Education," in 2021 for "Promising Young Woman" and in 2024 for "Maestro." She's also known for playing the iconic role of Daisy Buchanan in Baz Luhrman's glitzy 2013 adaptation of "The Great Gatsby." She and Isaac have worked together before, in the Coen Brothers' 2013 folk music film "Inside Llewyn Davis."Oscar Isaac as Josh Martin in "Beef."Who is Oscar Isaac? A Hollywood heartthrob who has played everyone from a "Star Wars" rebel to an eccentric tech billionaire ("Ex Machina") to the voice of a Spider-Man ("Spider-Man: Across the Spiderverse"), Isaac most recently won critical acclaim for Guillermo del Toro's "Frankenstein," in which he played the mad Dr. Victor Frankestein himself.The Gen Z young lovers: Cailee Spaeny and Charles Melton as Ashley and AustinThe witnesses to Lindsay and Josh's violent fight are two of Josh's country club employees: Ashley (Spaeny) and Austin (Melton), who were sent to their boss's house to return the wallet he left at work. Ashley and Austin are young and in love, newly engaged and optimistic, but starting to get beaten down by the realities of their financial future. They start to wonder how they can use the video of Josh and Lindsay fighting to their advantage.Cailee Spaeny as Ashley Miller in "Beef."Who is Cailee Spaeny? Spaeny's burgeoning career in Hollywood has exploded in recent years, after she appeared on critically acclaimed HBO drama "Mare of Easttown" in 2021. Since then she's played Priscilla Presley opposite Jacob Elordi in 2023 biopic "Priscilla" and appeared in major films "Civil War" (2024), "Alien: Romulus" (2024) and most recently in the star-packed "Knives Out" film "Wake Up Dead Man"(2025). And her career is just getting started.Charles Melton as Austin Davis in "Beef."Who is Charles Melton? The former "Riverdale" actor has graduated from his CW roots into major films and TV shows in recent years. In 2019 he was the male lead in YA drama "The Sun Is Also a Star," but offered a distinctly more mature, acclaimed performance alongside Julianne Moore and Natalie Portman in 2023's "May December." In 2025 he starred in "Warfare" alongside fellow future Hollywood leading men like Kit Connor, Noah Centineo and Joseph Quinn.The billionaire boss and her surgeon husband: Youn Yuh-jung and Song Kang-ho as Chairwoman Park and Dr. KimComplicating Josh, Austin and Ashley's employment at the country club is the arrival of Chairwoman Park (Youn), a South Korean billionaire who has recently bought the property and plans on making changes. She's married to Dr. Kim (Song), a famous South Korean plastic surgeon. Both figures start out on the periphery of the "Beef" story before the chaos starts to envelope them.Youn Yuh-jung as Chairwoman Park in "Beef."Who is Youn Yuh-jung? A South Korean actress with a deep resume in that country's film and television industry, Youn starred in Apple TV's 2022-2024 series "Pachinko," as well as Oscar-winning 2020 film "Minari." In fact, she's the one who won the Oscar, in the best supporting actress category. She starred in Minari alongside "Beef" Season 1 star Steven Yeun.Song Kang-ho as Dr. Kim in "Beef."Who is Song Kang-ho? American audience will recognize Song best from Oscar-winning film "Parasite" (2019) from acclaimed director Boon Jong-ho. He has collaborated with the director multiple times, including in celebrated horror film "The Host" (2006) and in the popular post-apocalyptic "Snowpiercer" (2013) appearing alongside Chris Evans.The country club elite: William Fitchner and Mikaela Hoover as Troy and AvaEvery country club has its stuck-up, entitled members, and Troy (Fitchner) and Ava (Hoover) exemplify the rich jerk trope for "Beef." Troy acts like Josh's friend, but sees him first and foremost as staff. Ava similarly buddies up to Lindsay without respecting her. (Look out for a few cameos from the real-life rich and famous in the show, too.)William Fichtner as Troy in "Beef."Who is William Fitchner? A hardworking actor you'll recognize from half a dozen films and TV shows, Fitchner is best known for major blockbusters like "Armageddon" (1998), "Black Hawk Down" (2001) and "The Accountant" (2011). You might have seen him more recently on CBS's sitcom "Mom" as Allison Janney's love interest.Mikaela Hoover as Ava in "Beef."Who is Mikaela Hoover? The actress has been working steadily in Hollywood for 20 years, mostly in guest roles on TV shows like "Two Broke Girls" and "Lucifer." She appeared as a regular on the WB's short-lived college drama "Sorority Forever" in 2008. But she's best known as the journalist Cat Grant in 2025's "Superman," sporting a platinum-blonde hairdo.The assistant and the tennis pro: Seoyeon Jang and Matthew Kim as Eunice and WooshIt's not just office politics that is causing tension at the club and for our lead couples, but also the appearance of two attractive new faces around the tennis courts making eyes at Austin and and Lindsay. Eunice (Jang) is Chairwoman Park's translator and assistant, and is not so soft-spoken and submissive as she originally appears. Aptly named Woosh (Kim) is the club's new hot tennis pro, flirting with all the women before trying to sell them skincare products and expensive laser treatments and surgeries from none other than Dr. Kim back in South Korea.Seoyeon Jang as Eunice in "Beef."Who is Seoyeon Jang? The actress has mostly made her career in Korean TV including "Butterfly" and "Hearbeat." "Beef" is her first major English-language role.Matthew Kim as Woosh in "Beef."Who is Matthew Kim? Better known as BM or Big Matthew, Kim is a K-Pop star making his acting debut in "Beef." He's worked with co-ed KPop group Kard, released his own solo music and worked as a composer.This article originally appeared on USA TODAY: The full 'Beef' Season 2 cast, from Oscar Isaac to a KPop idol
